subject: Simulating leaf temperature in NicheMapR (microclimate and ectotherm parameters)

messages.author: 055488460a2f9a4b
messages.subject: Simulating leaf temperature in NicheMapR (microclimate and ectotherm parameters)
parts:
Hi Mike,

I am using NicheMapR to simulate leaf temperature at a specific location over summer months of 2022-2023.

I have a few uncertainties regarding the input parameters:

1. For the microclimate model (micro_era5), I can't seem to increase the leaf height (Usrhyt) greater than 2 m. It appears I can't have a leaf height greater than the reference height (Refhy default = 2m). I would like to simulate a leaf on a tree - is it possible to  increase the height of the leaf beyond 2m? Say 5m.

2. For the ectotherm model, I am uncertain how to parametise the shape / size of the leaf using the proportionality factor (see below). I am guessing that for an leaf being an ellipsoid: b axis = length of the leaf surface, a axis = width of the leaf surface and c axis = thickness of leaf. But I am very unsure whether I have mixed up the a and b axis. 

  • shape_b = 3, Proportionality factor (-) for going from volume to area, represents ratio of width:height for a plate, length:diameter for cylinder, b axis:a axis for ellipsoid

  • shape_c = 0.6666666667, Proportionality factor (-) for going from volume to area, represents ratio of length:height for a plate, c axis:a axis for ellipsoid


Any advice would be much appreciated.

Thanks :) 
Lisa

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Simulating leaf temperature in NicheMapR (microclimate and ectotherm parameters)
parts:
Hi Lisa,

The microclimate model doesn't give you predictions above the reference height (which is the height at which the meteorological data was measured). But the new function get_profile which I just recently added to NicheMapR can predict to heights above the reference height - just wind speed which keeps increasing logarithmically according to what you put in for the wind shear exponent parameter 'a' (assuming air temperature/relative humidity don't change any more with height above the reference height).

Re the proportionality factor issue, if you're modelling an ellipsoid, you have three axes, 'a', 'b' and 'c'. For a prolate ellipsoid, 'a' is bigger than 'b' and 'c' and is called the 'semi-major axis'. For defining the shape you're assuming a = 1 and represents the length of the leaf, b is the thickness and c is the width, so you'd make b very small to have a thin leaf. In the example in the first appendix in the supporting material for the MEE paper the following is used:
Ww_g <- 1 # wet weight, g
shape <- 2 # 0=plate, 1=cylinder, 2=ellipsoid
shape_b <- 0.0025 # ratio of b axis:a axis for ellipsoid
shape_c <- 0.1176 # ratio of c axis:a axis for ellipsoid

Further down in the example the GEOM.ecto function is used to get some of the absolute geometric consequences of this choice of shape for a 1 g leaf:
GEOM.out <- GEOM_ecto(AMASS = Ww_g/1000, GEOMETRY = shape, SHP = c(1,
shape_b, shape_c), PTCOND = pct_cond/100, PMOUTH = 0, SKINW = 0/100)
w <- GEOM.out$AL/0.7 # leaf width, m
A <- GEOM.out$AREA # total leaf surface area, m2

Hope that helps.
All the best,
Mike
